findings.detail: declares openWorldHint=false but the handler makes network calls (api.request).
findings.note: declares READ_ONLY with open_world_hint=False and calls its own fixed gateway API. The author defines five constants and separates READ_ONLY from READ_EXTERNAL/WRITE_EXTERNAL, so the closed-world choice is deliberate. Per the spec a single known service is a closed domain; the rule 'any network call implies open world' is too strict. Debatable, counted against the detector.

findings.detail: declares readOnlyHint=true but the handler calls asyncio.create_subprocess_exec. Clients use this annotation to skip confirmation prompts.
findings.note: declares readOnlyHint=true; the subprocesses are curl with --proto =https --max-redirs 0 and a _html_worker that isolates CPU-heavy parsing from the event loop. Nothing in the caller's environment is modified. The detector conflates spawning a subprocess with mutating state, and penalises defensive engineering.
